title: Who Can Use Motorways (and Learners)
whatItIs: Traffic on motorways is fast, so you have less time to react. Some road users are not allowed on them at all.

keyFacts.text: Motorways MUST NOT be used by pedestrians, cyclists, horse riders or motorcycles under 50 cc.
Slow vehicles such as farm tractors, mobility scooters and powered wheelchairs MUST NOT use motorways.
Learner car drivers MUST NOT use motorways unless with an approved instructor in a dual-control car with L plates.
Learner motorcyclists MUST NOT use motorways.

keyFacts: Before a motorway trip, make sure you have enough fuel or charge, and plan time for breaks.

items.title: Pedestrians
items.text: Not allowed, except in an emergency.

items.title: Motorcycles under 50 cc
items.text: Not allowed on motorways, even with a full licence.

items.title: Slow vehicles
items.text: Farm tractors, mobility scooters and powered wheelchairs are not allowed.

items.title: Learner car drivers
items.text: Only with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.

items.title: Full licence holders
items.text: Cars, motorcycles of 50 cc or more, vans, lorries and buses.

onTheTest.question: Who can take a learner car driver on a motorway?
options: An approved driving instructor in a dual-control car
A parent who has held a licence for 3 years
Nobody: learners are banned from motorways
onTheTest.why: Since 2018, learner car drivers can have motorway lessons, but only with an approved driving instructor in a car with dual controls.

traps: Learners can't practise on a motorway with family or friends.
Learner motorcyclists still can't use motorways.
A motorcycle under 50 cc is banned, even with a full licence.

sources.ref: Driving lessons and learning to drive

jurisdictionNotes.text: In Wales learners can show D plates instead of L plates.
